dependency: The preferred dependency is sustained 900 rpm stirring until three successive five-second side-image checks have spread at most 4 percent, treated as necessary for uniformity. The stipulated 300 rpm final samples question that necessity for this bounded exercise, but do not identify why the 900 rpm images fluctuate. Examine the causal_return_path_hypothesis as an unobserved loop: agitation-generated optical disturbances could cause failed checks, which command further agitation and renew disturbances. The reversed causal arrow to test is that continued agitation produces the apparent evidence of incomplete mixing; the rival arrow is that actual incomplete mixing produces optical spread and continued stirring helps redistribute dye. Hypothetically sever the return link from optical spread to further stirring by using a predetermined 60-second 900 rpm run while logging the preferred rule in shadow mode. Compare with the enabled rule at the same nominal speed, capped at second 105. Hold initial demand fixed using the same 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye recipe, addition location, fresh rinsed vessel, dye bottle and locked camera settings; hold the valued outcome specification fixed at independent three-elevation sample spread at most 4 percent at second 120. These are proposed interventions, not observed successes.

predictions.account: Hypothesis: the optical-to-agitation return link sustains disturbances after the bounded sample outcome is already achievable.
predictions.when: In a proposed paired 900 rpm comparison, enable the preferred optical stop rule in one fresh trial and sever its command link in the other by stopping at a precommitted 60 seconds. Log shadow-rule decisions, duration, side spread, depression and specks. Both trials must stop by second 105, sample at second 120, and report every target failure.
predictions.result: If this account is correct and the 60-second run suffices, the severed trial would use less stirring despite shadow-rule failures, while both trials would meet the final-vial spread target. This would support a costly feedback dependency in this comparison; it would neither establish bubbles nor establish necessity or sufficiency for other trials.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: unresolved dye gradients cause optical spread, and additional agitation helps achieve the sample target.
predictions.when: Use the same proposed enabled-versus-severed 900 rpm pair, initial recipe and independent second-120 sample target.
predictions.result: If 60 seconds is inadequate under this rival account, the timer-stopped trial would retain final-vial spread above 4 percent while the longer enabled trial would achieve at most 4 percent. That outcome would favor useful additional mixing in this pair, but would not prove 900 rpm or the particular optical rule necessary. Failure of both would leave the accounts unresolved.

predictions.account: Hypothesis testing the reversed arrow: commanded agitation causes transient image disturbance rather than image spread necessarily indicating remaining concentration gradients.
predictions.when: In two proposed fixed-duration fresh trials, independently command 300 or 900 rpm for 60 seconds, remove optical control of duration, and compare images at matched elapsed times. After stopping at second 60, continue five-second image observations and take final vials at second 120 after the same 60-second quiet interval. Hold addition location fixed and record trial order.
predictions.result: Under this account, 900 rpm would produce greater transient spread, depression or speck counts while stirring; that spread would fall promptly after the commanded stop, and both final sample spreads could meet the target. The temporal response to an externally set stop would support an agitation-to-image effect. It would not alone identify the specks, establish uniformity before stopping, or demonstrate that the return loop actually operates.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: genuine gradients or a persistent optical artifact, rather than an agitation-renewed return mechanism, explain the image differences.
predictions.when: Use the proposed fixed-duration speed pair. If two trials remain within the six-trial session limit, repeat that pair in reverse speed order with a matched brief stir-off observation interval at seconds 45 to 50 in both runs; resume and stop at second 65 to keep total stirring at 60 seconds. Compare paused and moving frames at matched times, and compare final samples within each pair after its common quiet interval.
predictions.result: If genuine gradients dominate, brief cessation would not reliably remove elevation spread without redistribution, and remaining spread could accompany final-vial target failure. If a persistent optical artifact dominates, side-image spread could persist through cessation even while final samples meet the target. Neither pattern would support the specific disturbance-renewal loop by itself. Pauses change settling and transport, so a rapid image change would still require cautious interpretation.

surviving_outcome: The valued outcome is three elevation samples with normalized blue-channel attenuation spread at most 4 percent of their mean by second 120, with reduced stirring time if feasible. In the stipulated 300 rpm trial, stopping at second 60 produced final attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. Thus this synthetic sample-proxy outcome has already survived absence of sustained 900 rpm stirring in one observed case. That is a bounded counterexample to the asserted necessity, not causal evidence for bubble entrainment or the return loop. Future timer-controlled 900 rpm success remains a hypothesis; stable side images alone cannot establish success.
unknowns: No matched 900 rpm final-vial evidence establishes whether the stipulated fluctuating images coincide with sample gradients.
Bright specks may be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye; neither their identity nor their causal contribution is established, and bubble fraction cannot be measured with the supplied resources.
The observed checks do not establish actual rule-driven prolongation relative to a successful fixed-duration 900 rpm run; that comparison is proposed.
A rapid image response to stopping may reflect surface shape, settling or other optical changes and cannot identify bubbles or prove concentration uniformity before the common quiet interval.
Enabled and timer-stopped trials can have different total quiet durations before second 120. Record cessation times; this limits attribution of final-sample differences solely to additional stirring.

Sampling order and transfers can disturb gradients, nominal rpm has no independent verification, and common-aliquot repeatability is not optical concentration calibration. Alternate sampling order within pairs and report raw readings.
At most six trials are available; limited replication, order effects and reference repeatability constrain causal strength. Keep the spill tray in use and stop if liquid escapes.
Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit follows from this synthetic proxy.
